statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises (INPI) – https://guichet-unique.inpi.fr; RCS via Infogreffe; INPI name availability certificate
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French language required for public acts, advertising, and corporate designation under Loi n° 94-665 (Toubon); Latin script; 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' suffix mandatory; foreign words may be used if accompanied by French translation or explanation; no misleading or infringing names; transliteration from non-Latin script must be official and certified.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If INPI or greffe rejects the name, file a recours gracieux with INPI within two months; if maintained, file recours contentieux before the tribunal judiciaire de Paris or competent tribunal within two months. Alternatively, amend the name and refile. For infringement, opposition before INPI or court action. For RCS refusal, appeal to the greffe and then to the tribunal de commerce.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or domiciliation is permissible for an SARL if supported by a valid domiciliation contract under Code de commerce art. L.123-11-2 and Décret n° 2011-1016; however, tax and social security authorities may challenge if there is no effective place of management or commercial substance. For a digital-only micro-drama app, a business address with at least one substantive function is recommended; a pure virtual office may trigger tax residence or permanent establishment scrutiny.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate to high for a foreign-owned SARL with digital activity and a domiciliation-only address: estimated 15–30% annual probability of unannounced inspection by DGFiP, URSSAF, or greffe; lower (5–10%) if a physical office and local manager are present.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general company provisions) and Articles L.223-1 to L.223-57 (SARL); implementing Décret n° 2007-431, Articles R.223-1 et seq.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), in liaison with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Universal Declaration of Company Constitution (Déclaration de constitution d'une société) with annexed Articles of Association (Statuts)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital (Article L.223-2); the Articles may lawfully fix capital at €1. At least 20% of cash contributions must be paid up at subscription and 100% of in-kind contributions must be fully transferred before registration (Article L.223-7). Funds must be deposited in a dedicated blocked escrow bank account and certified by an attestation de dépôt des fonds.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING ASSOCIATES OF [COMPANY NAME] SARL, ADOPTED ON [DATE]

The founding associates hereby unanimously resolve: (1) to approve the final Articles of Association and authorize their signature; (2) to confirm the full subscription of the share capital of [€X], divided into [Y] shares, with at least twenty per cent of cash and all in-kind contributions paid up before registration; (3) to fix the registered office at [ADDRESS] and ratify the occupancy title; (4) to appoint [NAME] as Gérant for an indefinite term with full powers to bind the company; and (5) to delegate to the Gérant all authority to file the constitution dossier with the Guichet unique and to complete all ancillary formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Signing of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The founding associates, with optional assistance of a Notaire (mandatory only when a contribution in kind consists of real property)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts incorporating all mandatory legal clauses: corporate form (SARL), corporate name, registered office, corporate objects (production and global distribution of vertical micro-dramas), share capital, share count and nominal value, cash and in-kind contribution schedules, rights and obligations attached to shares, identity and powers of the Gérant, and corporate duration fixed at up to 99 years. Verify legal capacity of each associate. If any in-kind contribution exceeds the €7,500 statutory threshold, commission a commissaire aux apports valuation report. Have each associate sign the completed deed manually or by authenticated electronic signature, or by proxy pursuant to a signed power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Final draft of Articles of Association (Statuts)
Valid passport or national ID of each associate
Proof of residential address of each associate (issued within the last 3 months)
Notarized power of attorney, if an associate signs by proxy
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (only if in-kind contributions exceed €7,500)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notaire or registry queries signature admissibility or a defective clause, convene the associates to initial and re-seal the corrected deed and file a rectificative act through the Guichet unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Escrowed Capital Bank Account and Capital Deposit (Dépôt des Fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A credit institution established in the European Economic Area and supervised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the draft statuts and required KYC documents to the chosen bank. Open a temporary non-operational account in the name of the company 'en formation'. Transfer the committed funds, representing at least 20% of cash contributions plus 100% of any agreed cash-based callable funding, and obtain the attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital blocking certificate) evidencing that the funds are frozen until the company is registered in the RCS.
required_dossiers: Project of Articles of Association
Passport or ID and KYC documentation of all signatories
Declaration of beneficial owners
Source-of-funds evidence (salary slips, sale deeds, tax notices) satisfying AML due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank blocks the account on AML grounds, supply additional documented source-of-funds evidence to the bank's compliance officer; upon final refusal, escalate within the bank's internal appeals process or open the deposit with a second credit institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the Incorporation Notice (Avis de Constitution) in a Legal Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) authorized to publish in the department in which the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the avis de constitution containing the mandatory particulars under Article R.210-3 of the Commercial Code: corporate name, legal form, share capital amount, registered office address, corporate objects summary, duration, and the RCS court of registration. Deliver the draft to the JAL either online or by email, pay the publication fee, and obtain the attestation de parution (publication receipt) prior to filing the constitution dossier with the Guichet unique.
required_dossiers: Legal announcement draft signed by the Gérant or an authorized associate
Proof of payment of the JAL publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published notice contains an error, promptly order a rectificative avis in the same JAL and retain both receipts; a late or missing attestation de parution can be cured by securing an expedited certified copy from the JAL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of the Constitution Dossier to the Guichet Unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a user account on the official portal, select the company-creation workflow for a commercial entity (SARL), complete the universal declaration form with corporate information, SIREN assignment request, registered office address, share capital details, Gérant identity, and trade-activity classification (NAF/APE code 5911A). Upload all mandatory attachments in PDF, pay the state filing fee electronically, and submit. The portal automatically dispatches the dossier to the competent Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce, INSEE, URSSAF, DGFiP, and the CCI, after which the applicant receives an electronic acknowledgement of filing.
required_dossiers: Completed universal declaration form (formalité de création d'entreprise)
Signed Articles of Association (Statuts) in PDF
Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital blocking certificate)
Justification of the registered office occupancy (lease, title deed, or domiciliation agreement)
Attestation de parution au Journal d'Annonces Légales
Sworn declaration of no criminal conviction disqualifying the Gérant
Certified copy of passport or ID of the Gérant and each associate
Beneficial owner declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Guichet unique returns an 'incomplete' status, supply the identified attachments or amendments within the legal 15-day cure period. In case of repeated non-conformity or refusal, file an appeal against the refusal before the President of the Commercial Court having jurisdiction over the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Review and Issuance of the Kbis Extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce having jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the dossier from the Guichet unique, the Greffe verifies the legal regularity of the statuts, checks the corporate name against the National RCS database for prior rights, confirms the Gérant's eligibility against judicial disqualification registers, and enters the company in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés. The registry then issues the Kbis extract, which is the official identity certificate of the company and contains the assigned SIREN, SIRET, and NAF/APE code.
required_dossiers: Complete electronic constitution dossier transmitted by the Guichet unique
Receipt confirming payment of the official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe refuses registration on grounds of corporate-name conflict, adopt an amending resolution changing the name and re-file; if the refusal raises no legitimate legal basis, contest it within the applicable time limit before the President of the Commercial Court by way of a formal petition.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Social, Fiscal, and Auxiliary Activations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INSEE, URSSAF, Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), and the Greffe for the Beneficial Owners Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of Kbis issuance, verify the SIREN/SIRET identifiers and the official NAF code (5911A). Activate the company's professional bank account using the Kbis, register with URSSAF for employer and social-security obligations, elect the applicable VAT regime (franchise en base de TVA or réel) with the competent fiscal authority, confirm registration for the territorial economic contribution (CET), and complete the beneficial-owner register maintenance at the Greffe. Also log occupational-health obligations including the signature of the first service contract with a work-medicine provider.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract issued by the Greffe
Final signed Articles of Association
Professional bank account master agreement and RIB
Beneficial owner registry declaration (RBE form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If URSSAF or DGFiP activation messages are not received within the expected period, contact the respective URSSAF center or DRFIP with the Kbis and a written reactivation request; missing or erroneous SIRET data is rectified through a correction request submitted to INSEE via the Guichet unique.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Centre National du Cinéma et de l'Image Animée (CNC) and Autorité de régulation de la communication audiovisuelle et numérique (ARCOM)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration of the production company in the CNC Registre du cinéma et de l'audiovisuel (production category), and Declaration of On-Demand Audiovisual Media Service (Service de Médias Audiovisuels à la Demande) filed with ARCOM under Article 33-2 of Law n° 86-1067 of 30 September 1986

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) of the registered office region, under the Ministry of Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is not listed in the Annex to Article R.122-2 of the French Environment Code; purely tertiary digital content production and streaming operations do not trigger a full environmental impact assessment or prior environmental authorization
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharges to water or air are generated by the office/streaming activity; compliance with the EU WEEE Directive (2012/19/EU) applies to discarded electronic equipment; if a physical filming studio is later operated, verification must be made against the ICPE nomenclature (Code de l'environnement, Article R.511-9) to ensure any declared installations remain below the registration threshold for combustion or solvent-using equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the Code de la construction et de l'habitation for tertiary workplaces: functional fire extinguishers, evacuation plan, emergency lighting, smoke detection, and fire-resistant furnishing materials; if the premises receive visiting cast or third parties as studios or screening areas, the site must be declared as an ERP of the 5th category to the local Mairie and pass the consultative safety visit. Occupational clearance under the Code du travail: registration of employees with URSSAF, subscription with a Service de Prévention et de Santé au Travail for medical surveillance, and establishment of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) covering work on screens, acoustic stress, and filming-site movement risks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des finances publiques (DGFiP), principally through the Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE); official online portals include impots.gouv.fr, the professional tax account (Espace professionnel), and the business formalities portal at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr. French customs matters are administered by the Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects (DGDDI), principally through douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A French SARL is registered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI). Upon registration, the entity receives an identification number (SIREN), an establishment number (SIRET), and an activity code (APE/NAF). The company must activate its professional tax account with the DGFiP and register for corporate income tax, payroll taxes where applicable, and VAT where required. The French VAT identification number is generally formatted as FR followed by a two-digit control key and the nine-digit SIREN. A foreign entity without a French establishment applies to the appropriate non-resident or business tax service and submits incorporation documents, constitutional documents, proof of business activity, identity and authority documents for representatives, French bank or commercial evidence where requested, and evidence of the French taxable transactions. A non-EU business generally must appoint a French fiscal representative for VAT purposes unless an applicable mutual-assistance arrangement or statutory exemption applies. An EU-established business generally does not need a French fiscal representative but must complete French VAT registration procedures. For EU cross-border goods transactions, an EORI number is obtained from French customs where required. Digital platform sales through Apple App Store, Google Play, or payment processors do not by themselves eliminate the company's responsibility to determine its French and EU VAT obligations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A SARL is ordinarily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, or IS). An eligible SARL may elect temporarily for income-tax treatment (impôt sur le revenu, or IR), generally for up to five fiscal years, subject to statutory conditions concerning ownership, size, age, activity, and shareholder composition; the election is not a general check-the-box election. A qualifying family SARL may elect for IR treatment without the ordinary five-year limitation, subject to applicable conditions. There is no general US-style check-the-box regime in France. French anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implement the EU ATAD framework and may deny deductions, include income, or restrict relief; they do not create a general entity-classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, or TVA), integrated with EU VAT rules. Cross-border digital and electronically supplied services may also be reported through the EU One Stop Shop (OSS) regime where applicable.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France has no single universal VAT registration threshold. The domestic franchise en base de TVA may apply to eligible small businesses below the applicable annual turnover limits. For services and non-commercial activities, the principal threshold is generally EUR 37,500, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 41,250; for trading, sales, and accommodation activities, the principal threshold is generally EUR 85,000, with a tolerance threshold generally of EUR 93,500. Thresholds are subject to statutory indexing, legislative amendments, activity classification, and special regimes. Businesses making intra-EU acquisitions, imports, exports, reverse-charge transactions, electronically supplied services, or transactions requiring a VAT invoice may require VAT identification irrespective of domestic franchise thresholds. A business exceeding the relevant threshold or voluntarily opting into VAT must register and comply from the applicable effective date.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France has mandatory electronic invoicing for transactions involving French-established taxable businesses and the public sector under the applicable public-procurement and Chorus Pro framework. The private-sector rollout is scheduled in phases: all businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices from 1 September 2026; issuance obligations generally apply to large and intermediate businesses from 1 September 2026 and to small and medium-sized businesses and micro-enterprises from 1 September 2027, subject to legislative and regulatory implementation. Invoices will generally be transmitted through an approved private electronic invoicing platform or the public portal designated by law. France is adopting structured invoice data and separate electronic reporting of relevant transaction and payment data; this is not a universal real-time pre-clearance model comparable to Italy's SDI for every domestic invoice. Digital invoice integrity, authenticity, readability, retention, VAT invoice fields, and audit-trail requirements remain mandatory. App-store statements, payment-processor reports, and platform settlement records should be reconciled with the company's VAT books and supporting transaction data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: French VAT law generally treats qualifying exports of goods from France to a destination outside the EU as VAT-exempt with a right of deduction, rather than technically as a domestic 0% rate. The supplier must establish that the goods left the EU customs territory and that the transaction satisfies the export conditions. Evidence normally includes the export customs declaration, the electronic exit result or equivalent customs proof, transport documentation, commercial invoices, and a consistent audit trail linking the goods, customer, carrier, customs declaration, and payment. Intra-EU supplies of goods may be exempt where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are dispatched to that Member State, and the supplier retains transport and VAT-number evidence. Services are not automatically export zero-rated. B2B services are generally located where the business customer is established and may be outside French VAT, often under customer reverse charge. B2C electronically supplied services are generally taxable in the customer's jurisdiction; EU consumer transactions may be reported through OSS, while non-EU consumer supplies require analysis under the destination country's rules. Production, licensing, streaming, advertising, and platform-distribution revenue must be classified separately because place-of-supply and exemption outcomes differ.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export customs declaration or electronic export record containing the Movement Reference Number (MRN), where applicable
Electronic customs exit confirmation or other legally acceptable proof that the goods exited the EU customs territory
Commercial invoice and contract or order documentation identifying the supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and destination
Transport evidence, such as bill of lading, airway bill, CMR consignment note, courier record, or carrier delivery documentation
Packing list and, where relevant, export licences, certificates of origin, or product-specific regulatory documents
Supplier's French VAT identification number and, where relevant, EORI number

Payment and accounting records linking the export transaction to the customs and transport documents; an inward remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory French export-VAT document but may be relevant as supplementary commercial evidence or under the law of the destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France does not generally impose a universal 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline as a condition for export VAT exemption or refund. Export proceeds should nevertheless be traceable through accounting, banking, customs, and contractual records. If the taxpayer cannot substantiate export conditions, the DGFiP may deny the exemption or refund, reassess output VAT, recover improperly deducted input VAT, and charge late-payment interest. Tax penalties may include a 10% late-filing or late-payment surcharge, a 40% penalty for deliberate failure, and an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or certain abusive conduct, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards. Customs violations may trigger duty and tax recovery, customs penalties, confiscation, and potentially criminal liability. Deliberate VAT fraud may also lead to criminal prosecution. Records should generally be retained for the applicable statutory audit period, commonly at least six years for VAT documentation, with longer retention where commercial, customs, accounting, or litigation rules require it.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), with ultimate monetary authority vested in the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro-area policy. Prudential supervision and licensing of credit institutions is delegated to the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), which operates under the Banque de France's umbrella. All euro payment infrastructure (TARGET2, Eurosystem) is accessible to the SARL through its French settlement bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility. France operates a liberalized exchange-control regime compliant with EU Treaty obligations (TFEU Articles 63-65 on free movement of capital) and OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Both current-account flows (royalties, service fees, profits) and capital-account flows (equity injections, shareholder loans, loan repayments, sale of shares) are freely convertible without prior exchange-control approval. No specific exchange rate regime restrictions apply; the euro trades freely. Profit remittance by a French SARL is subject only to standard corporate formalities (shareholder resolution and distributable-reserve tests under French commercial law) and applicable anti-money-laundering documentation; no exchange control tax or levy is imposed. France applies no spin-off specific restrictions on distribution of dividends to non-resident shareholders; any withholding taxes are governed solely by domestic tax law and the applicable tax treaty (e.g., France-China DTA). Transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 moving across the border (including inbound capital contributions) are reportable to Banque de France for balance-of-payments statistics; this is a post-transaction statistical filing, not a restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. France has no mandatory export proceeds surrender or repatriation obligation for merchandise or services exporters. The SARL may retain export proceeds in foreign currency onshore or offshore at its discretion; no forced conversion into EUR, no statutory timeline for bringing proceeds onshore, and no mandatory conversion ratio exists. The only ancillary condition is the balance-of-payments statistical declaration to Banque de France (via the bank or direct filing) for any single cross-border transaction equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500, and the annual 'liaison financière' direct-investment survey where a foreign shareholder holds 10% or more of the SARL's capital or voting rights. These are informational duties, not surrender or exchange-approval requirements.

Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / franchised 'Société Générale Business' digital onboarding channel

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for operational use but low sufficiency as the sole or primary account. ACPR-licensed French electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Manager.one, and Shine offer efficient onboarding (fully remote, 24-hour approvals) and are suitable as collection/disbursement workhorses, including multi-currency pockets. Non-French EU EMIs (Revolut Business, Wise Business, Pliant) operate under passporting and can open accounts for a French SARL; their viability is High for treasury operations (low-cost FX, virtual cards) but Medium on compliance confidence because certain EMI accounts are geoblocked for App Store merchant registration and some French tax authorities (and counterparties) prefer an account held with a credit institution rather than with an EMI under the French 'droit au compte' regime. Legal constraint: for the statutory capital deposit attestation required to incorporate or increase the capital of a SARL, only a bank established in France (credit institution), a notary, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations can issue the blocking certificate; an EMI cannot. EMIs must not be relied upon for the capital escrow account. Additionally, the SARL benefits from the French statutory right to a bank account (Code monétaire et financier, Arts. L312-1 et seq.): if two banks refuse onboarding, Banque de France designates a bank; this right is exercised through ACPR, and it materially guarantees the SARL's access to payment services regardless of the EMI debate.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Permitted fully remotely by all major French banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, CIC) via video KYC (usually an asynchronous identity scan plus a recorded video call) for the SARL's legal representative (gérant), provided the gérant holds a valid EU/EEA passport or a French residence permit and the corporate documents are electronic. If the gérant is a resident of China or another non-EU jurisdiction, remote opening is usually conditionally permitted: the bank will require notarized and apostilled (Convention de la Haye) statutes, an apostilled resolution appointing the gérant, a notarized copy of the passport, and a third-party financial reference; a live video interview is typically mandatory, and certain regional banks may require one physical visit to the branch or to a French foreign trade office (e.g., in Hong Kong or Singapore via BNP Paribas Fortis, SocGen's international network). A purely remote onboarding is, however, the rule for a standard low-risk micro-drama operating SARL with French-resident representation. We recommend appointing a French-resident gérant to de-risk the process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident (Chinese) ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and a gérant who is a foreign tax resident: the bank's sanctions and PEP screening flags source-of-wealth opacity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copy notarized and apostilled (or Chinese consular legalization); certificate of tax residence from the PRC tax authority (or the UBO's jurisdiction); 6 months of personal bank statements proving the origin of the capital injection; a sworn source of wealth letter; corporate registry extract and structure chart of the ultimate shareholder; banking reference letter from the originating bank in the UBO's home jurisdiction; clean sanctions check via OFAC/EU/UK consolidated lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Micro-cap SARL (e.g., EUR 10-100 share capital) with an outsized international growth forecast for a content-streaming operation: the bank assesses viability gap and potentially flags the company as a 'mailbox' or insolvency risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Drafted statutes with real registered office lease (not domiciliation at a virtual address); full business plan with 24-month cash-flow forecasts; signed content-distribution agreements (short-drama licenses); platform showroom references; contractual commitments from Apple/Google developers' programmes; evidence of a dedicated professional liability/errors & omissions policy; management CVs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Recurring material outbound payments to content producers, scriptwriters, influencers and advertising agencies in various jurisdictions (including possibly high-risk or sanctioned-adjacent territories) with no clear documentary chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standardized production/service agreements with defined deliverables; itemized invoices with valid EU VAT numbers where applicable; sub-license and IP chain title registry; pre-payment provider KYC questionnaire; sanctions/denied-party screening evidence for each counterparty; a covenant in templates preventing dealing with sanctioned parties or sanctioned territories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-heavy business model: the bank questions whether the SARL actually owns or is licensed to exploit the 'vertical micro-drama' catalogue (IP title risk leading to business continuity concerns).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Copyright registration certificates (or accepted deposits) from the US Copyright Office and/or French Centre National du Cinéma (CNC) for the works; title-chain agreements and chain-of-title opinion from a French IP attorney; the public listing of works at the Société des Auteurs et Compositeurs Dramatiques (SACD) if the SARL registers authors, or a clean independent-creation declaration; warranty and indemnity clauses in acquisition agreements relating to the catalogue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The inbound capital injection originates from a Chinese shareholder subject to PRC State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) ODI approval; if the transfer is routed via a Hong Kong/digital-asset intermediary, the French bank will raise a funds-origin red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE ODI filing certificate (企业境外直接投资外汇登记) of the Chinese shareholder; the bank transfer through a cleared banking corridor (HK or Luxembourg intermediary) with full SWIFT reference; correspondent-bank attestation; the SARL's registration of the foreign investment (liaison financière) with Banque de France; an anti-fraud/receipt acknowledgment from the SARL; the parent company's audited financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual consolidated decision of SARL shareholders approving the financial statements and statutory deposit of the annual accounts (depot des comptes annuels) together with the management report (rapport de gestion)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) filed electronically via the INPI Guichet Unique e-management platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval must occur within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (e.g., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); the approved accounts must be deposited at the registry within 2 months of approval (i.e., by 31 August for a calendar-year closing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil enforcement proceeds by injunction of the Commercial Court President to file within one month under a coercive daily penalty (astreinte); maximum civil fines of EUR 15,000 for a legal entity and EUR 5,000 for an individual legal representative; non-compliance is recorded in the open registry file and can lead to administrative strike-off (radiation) after summons

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (liasse fiscale; forms 2065-SD and annexes) for the SARL subject to corporate income tax (IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP - Service des Impots des Entreprises (SIE) of the registered office; mandatory electronic filing via the e-company/efile portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing by 3 May of the following calendar year for a 31 December year-end; for an off-schedule fiscal close, within the 3rd month following the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic late-filing surcharge of 5% of the net tax due (raised to 10% if not regularised within 30 days of formal notice), plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.40% from the original due date; refunds and tax clearance certificates are blocked until the return is filed

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial ownership declaration (declaration des beneficiaires effectifs - DBE) and updated copy of the beneficial owners register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (annual lodgment with the accounts; the register itself is kept at the SARL registered office for inspection by AML, tax and judicial authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually at the same time as the annual accounts deposit (typically between 1 June and 30 August for a calendar-year closing); any qualifying change in beneficial ownership (e.g., share transfer granting at least 25% of capital or voting rights, or control) must be declared within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 150 for late declaration; false, incomplete or misleading declarations carry fines up to EUR 7,500 for individuals and EUR 37,500 for legal entities, in addition to AML/Tracfin referral

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local business property tax (cotisation fonciere des entreprises - CFE) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DDFiP - Service des Impots des Entreprises of the municipality where the SARL registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payment due by 15 December of the tax year (prior-year tax above EUR 3,000 triggers a 15 June instalment and 15 December balance); exemption applies for the first 2 years of activity; if the company has no commercial premises, a minimum or reduced municipal base is assessed in the November notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic 10% increase on the unpaid amount after 15 December, monthly late interest of 0.20%, and enforcement by tax lien (privilege du Tresor), enforceable notice (avis de mise en recouvrement) and bank account seizure against the streaming company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is required for a micro vertical-drama SARL unless at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: balance-sheet total at least EUR 4.2 million; net turnover excluding VAT at least EUR 8.4 million; average workforce of at least 50 employees. Appointment can also be requested by shareholders holding at least 1/10 of the SARL share capital
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable General - PCG) as codified in Reglement ANC n. 2014-03 and its amendments; the micro-entity simplification regime (art. L123-16-1 C. com.) applies below EUR 700,000 net turnover, EUR 350,000 balance-sheet total and 10 employees; IFRS is not permitted for the SARL statutory individual financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The beneficial owners register must be permanently available at the registered office. The annual filing protocol imposes: (i) a yearly DBE confirmation lodged with the greffe when the annual accounts are deposited, and (ii) a 30-day corrective declaration after any share transfer that causes a new person to hold at least 25% of share capital or voting rights, or to exercise control. The UBO register must be aligned with the last DBE before any share transfer, bank financing or notarial transaction

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250 - USD 800 per year for third-party domiciliation and registered-office services (Paris and Ile-de-France positioning at the upper end; provincial micro-SARLs at the lower end)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 per engagement (only triggered if the SARL exceeds the mandatory audit thresholds or voluntarily appoints a commissaire aux comptes; micro-drama SARLs normally pay no audit fee)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax effective for fiscal years closing on or after 31 December 2022)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small SARLs pay 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per fiscal year; the balance is taxed at 25%. No statutory tax holiday. Available incentives include the audiovisual production tax credit (credit d'impot pour la production d'oeuvres audiovisuelles, approximately 20% of eligible French production expenditure) and expensing of qualifying original content costs, subject to administrative approval.
